issues.description: The problem statement's UML declares ExcellenceLand.excellencyLevel as int (problem_statement.md line 35), but the solution implements excellencyLevel as double (solution_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/ExcellenceLand.java lines 7 and 11). This creates a type mismatch for the attribute, its constructor parameter and its getter return type. Students following the UML (or the textual task) will declare an int, while the reference solution and its constructor use a double, which may cause test failures or confusion about the correct type.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the type for excellencyLevel consistent across artifacts. Either change the solution to use int for excellencyLevel (update the field, constructor parameter and getter to int) to match the UML/problem statement, or update the problem statement/UML to specify double if a floating-point level was intended. Prefer keeping the UML/task and solution aligned (recommended: change the solution to int).
